braze-flutter-sdk #142 [open] [Feature]: Deprecating BrazePlugin.initBraze(_:) is problematic for Add-to-App projects
## What problem are you facing? ### Summary As of [v18.0.0](https://pub.dev/packages/braze_plugin/changelog#1800), `BrazePlugin.initBraze(_:)` is deprecated in favor of `BrazePlugin.configure(_:postInitialization:)` combined with `initialize(apiKey, endpoint)` on the Dart side. For an app, which uses an Add-to-App architecture (a native iOS host with an embedded Flutter module), the removal of `BrazePlugin.initBraze(_:)` would introduce a problem. This issue describes that problem and asks for guidance. ### Why the removal of `initBraze` is a problem for us Today we call `initBraze` in `AppDelegate`, so a single Braze instance is created at app launch and shared by both the native and the Flutter side — the Flutter side never calls `initialize()`. Under the new flow, the instance is instead created by `initialize()` from Dart, which cannot run until the Flutter engine is up. In our app, that is not at launch. If `initBraze` is no longer available, we are left with one of two options, and neither works well for us: **Option 1: Defer Braze initialization until a Flutter screen is opened** Problem: Braze features that the native side relies on immediately after launch (push, in-app messages, Banners, and so on) would be unavailable from app launch until the user opens a Flutter screen. **Option 2: Start the Flutter engine at app launch solely to call `initialize()`** Problem: In an Add-to-App architecture, the native host starts first and the Flutter engine starts only when a Flutter screen is needed. Under the new flow, initializing Braze at launch would require starting the Flutter engine at launch as well, abandoning that lazy startup for the sake of a single SDK. ## Workarounds We continue using the deprecated `BrazePlugin.initBraze(_:)` in `AppDelegate` at launch. The Flutter side never calls `initialize()`. It works today, but shows deprecation warnings and may break in a future release. ## Ideal Solution A non-deprecated API with the same behavior as `initBraze`

braze-cordova-sdk #108 [open] Expose DISPLAY_LATER (defer + replay) for in-app messages via the Cordova/Capacitor bridge
## Summary Please expose the native **`DISPLAY_LATER`** in-app message operation through the Cordova/Capacitor JS bridge. Today the plugin only bridges a `useBrazeUI` boolean, which maps to `DISPLAY_NOW` (true) or `DISCARD` (false). There is no way for the JS layer to tell Braze "**don't show this now, but keep it and let me re-request it later**" — which the native Android and Swift SDKs fully support via `InAppMessageOperation.DISPLAY_LATER` / `BRZInAppMessageUIDisplayChoiceLater`. ## Environment - Plugin: `@braze/cordova-sdk` (also used in Capacitor + Ionic apps) - Platforms affected: iOS and Android - Relevant API: `subscribeToInAppMessage(successCallback, errorCallback, useBrazeUI)` ## The Problem We need to **suppress in-app messages on sensitive/unsafe screens** (PIN entry, biometric prompt, onboarding, QR scanner, external WebView) and **show them once the user returns to a safe screen** — without losing the message. With the current bridge, our only options are: 1. **`useBrazeUI = true`** → Braze renders immediately, even over the PIN/biometric screen. Not acceptable. 2. **`useBrazeUI = false`** → the message is **DISCARDED**. It is permanently lost; flipping back to `true` later does **not** replay it. Braze does not re-serve it unless the campaign has re-eligibility enabled (off by default), and for session-start–triggered campaigns it won't re-fire until a new session. Neither option supports the standard **defer-and-replay** pattern that the native SDKs document and support out of the box. ## Why the current workarounds are insufficient - **Toggle DISPLAY_NOW/DISCARD** loses any message that fires while on an unsafe screen. Relying on campaign re-eligibility is a fragile cross-team dependency and doesn't cover session-start triggers in the same session. - **`useBrazeUI = false` + custom rendering:** the message JSON *is* delivered to the JS callback, so we can queue and re-render it ourselves. But this forces us to **rebuild the entire in-app message UI

Launch the app and let it run. The SDK opens the DUST SSE stream and reads it line-by-line. 3. Wait for the SSE connection to hit EOF (e.g. load-balancer idle timeout or any server-side close) **while the subscription is still considered active**. 4. On our test device this reproduced on every app launch within minutes, and the combined CPU + GC pressure contributed to an input-dispatch ANR on an emulator. ### Expected Behavior When the DUST stream hits EOF, the consumer should terminate the producer coroutine (close the channel) and/or reconnect with backoff through the existing reconnect logic. ### Actual Incorrect Behavior The stream consumer busy-loops forever re-reading the dead `BufferedReader` with no delay, pegging one CPU core and generating constant garbage (the charset decoder is flushed/reset on every iteration). braze-android-sdk #113 [open] [Bug]: OOM from pending-event storage — full-map re-serialization per event + runBlocking writes (reproduced on 40.1.1 and 43.0.0)
### Braze Android SDK Version 40.1.1 (also reproduced on 43.0.0) ### Steps To Reproduce 1. Log custom events faster than dispatch drains them — e.g. ~10-15 events/sec while scrolling a feed with impression tracking. Dispatch drains at most 32 events per request (sustained ~1 request/30s under the server-delivered rate limit), so the pending-event map grows without bound (verified past 2MB / 8,000+ events — no cap observed). It persists across sessions. 2. Keep logging once the map is ~1.5MB+: the heap fills with dozens of concurrent full-copy serializations of the map (each a map-sized char[]), each pinned by a parked runBlocking worker on the shared coroutine pool. 3. Restart the app with a large persisted map: the heap reaches ~106MB within 44 seconds of launch from the same mechanism. Why this happens (verified via bytecode of 40.1.1 and 43.0.0): - All pending events are stored under a single DataStore preferences key as one serialized JSON map (`{uuid: eventJson}`). - Every `logCustomEvent` triggers: read whole map → add one event → re-serialize the ENTIRE map → commit via `runBlocking` (`DataStoreProvider.write$android_sdk_base_release`). ### Expected Behavior Logging an event should have O(event) cost: appending one event should not re-serialize the entire pending store, should not block shared pool threads with runBlocking, and heap usage should stay flat regardless of how many events are queued. Per-event keys or append-only storage with non-blocking commits would achieve this — similar in spirit to the 43.0.0 fix for synchronous disk I/O in Card.logImpression(). ### Actual Incorrect Behavior Measured on 40.1.1: with a 1.9MB pending map, Dalvik PSS climbs to ~311MB with 71 blocked DefaultDispatcher-worker threads; ~67% of a 400MB heap dump is dozens of concurrent full copies of the map, each pinned by a parked runBlocking worker. Production apps at the 512MB largeHeap limit crash with OutOfMemoryError — worst right after launch, since the persisted map immed

### What problem are you facing? ## Description Starting with Android Gradle Plugin (AGP) 9.0, support for applying the Kotlin Gradle Plugin (KGP) has been removed. Because `braze_plugin` applies KGP in its Android build configuration, it causes the following warning at build time with Flutter 3.41+: WARNING: Your app uses the following plugins that apply Kotlin Gradle Plugin (KGP): braze_plugin Future versions of Flutter will fail to build if your app uses plugins that apply KGP. Flutter has temporarily added support to allow KGP while apps and plugins migrate to AGP 9.0+, but this support will be removed in a future version of Flutter (when AGP 10.0 becomes the default). ### Ideal Solution Please migrate this plugin to use built-in Kotlin to ensure your plugin users can successfully build their apps in future versions of Flutter. In `BrazePlugin.swift`, the implementation does: ```swift if let tokenData = token.data(using: .utf8) { BrazePlugin.braze?.notifications.register(deviceToken: tokenData) } ``` The token passed from Dart is a hex-encoded string representing the raw APNS device token. `.data(using: .utf8)` converts it to the ASCII byte representation of that hex string, not the actual token bytes. **Impact**: registerPushToken is completely non-functional on iOS. Push tokens register without error on the client side, but all push notifications fail delivery. Content cards and other Braze features work fine since they don't depend on the APNS token. **Steps to reproduce** 1. get apns token on iOS, such as by calling `firebaseMessaging.getAPNSToken()` or by doing this and passing it to flutter via a method channel ``` override func application(_ application: UIApplication, didRegisterForRemoteNotificationsWithDeviceToken deviceToken: Data) { let token = deviceToken.map { String(format: "%02x", $0) }.joined() } ``` 2. call `brazePlugin.registerPushToken(token)` with the string representation of a token. ### Expected Behavior The hex string should be decoded to its binary representation before being passed to register(deviceToken:). Something like: ```swift case "registerPushToken": guard let args = call.arguments as? [String: Any], let token = args["pushToken"] as? String else { return } var tokenData = Data() var index = token.startIndex while index < token.endIndex { let nextIndex = token.index(index, offsetBy: 2) if let byte =

Observe the following warning in the build log: ``` warning: The CFBundleShortVersionString of an app extension (null) must match that of its containing parent app ('2.4.1'). ``` ### Expected Behavior The `BrazeExpoRichPush` notification service extension's `CFBundleShortVersionString` should match the parent app's version string (e.g. `2.4.1`). The build should produce no version mismatch warning, and App Store submission should succeed. ### Actual Incorrect Behavior `CFBundleShortVersionString` resolves to null, causing this warning during the build ``` › Signing MyApp » MyApp.app The CFBundleShortVersionString of an app extension (null) must match that of its containing parent app ('2.4.1'). ``` ### Verbose Logs ```shell ``` ### Additional Information ## Root Cause The template plist used to generate the extension's `Info.plist` contains the wrong Xcode build variable: **`ios/ExpoAdapterBraze/RichPush/BrazeExpoRichPush-Info.plist`** ```xml <key>CFBundleShortVersionString</key> <string>$(CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION)</string> <!-- ← should be $(MARKETING_VERSION) --> <key>CFBundleVersion</key> <string>1</string> ``` `$(CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION)` is the **build number** variable. `CFBundleShortVersionString` requires `$(MARKETING_VERSION)`. The fix is a one-line change: ```diff <key>CFBundleShortVersionString</key> -<string>$(CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION)</string> +<string>$(MARKETING_VERSION)</string> ``` ## Workaround Solution Use a `withFinalizedMod` config plugin to patch the generated p

### What problem are you facing? Problem Summary: > Currently, the Braze Swift SDK does not explicitly support or provide binaries sliced for the `arm64e` architecture. - **Impact:** > While the SDK runs on `arm64`, it cannot take advantage of **Pointer Authentication Codes (PAC**), which are a key security feature of the `arm64e` architecture found in Apple's A12 Bionic chips and later. For high-security applications or projects that aim to compile entirely for `arm64e` to ensure maximum performance and hardware-level protection against memory corruption bugs, the lack of `arm64e` support in the SDK prevents a full-architecture build. My project requires strict architecture alignment for security and performance optimizations (Pointer Authentication). Since the Braze XCFramework only provides `arm64`. When attempting to build a project with "Build Active Architecture Only" set to No and targeting arm64e, the linker may throw errors regarding missing slices for the Braze library. ### Workarounds **Current Status:** > None. I have not implemented a workaround because excluding the architecture is not an option for our production requirements. Currently, the project fails to build entirely when `arm64e` is enabled in the build settings. The only "fix" at the moment is to downgrade the entire project's architecture requirements to `arm64`, which bypasses the security benefits of the A12+ chips that we intend to utilize. ### Ideal Solution Include the `arm64e` slice on XCFramework ### Other Information _No response_

braze-react-native-sdk #308 [closed] [Feature]: Add configurable timeout for getContentCards() method
### What problem are you facing? The `getContentCards()` method currently lacks a built-in timeout mechanism, which can lead to indefinite loading states in poor network conditions. ```javascript // This promise can hang indefinitely const cards = await Braze.getContentCards(); ``` - No timeout parameter available - No automatic rejection after X seconds - Forces developers to implement manual timeout workarounds In production apps, users on slow connections (3G, congested networks, corporate firewalls) may experience: - Infinite loading spinners - Poor user experience - Unable to access cached content while waiting ### Workarounds We're forced to implement manual timeouts: ```javascript timeoutRef.current = setTimeout(() => setIsLoading(false), 5000); ``` ### Ideal Solution ```javascript // Option 1: Global configuration Braze.configure({ contentCardsTimeout: 5000 // milliseconds }); // Option 2: Per-call configuration const cards = await Braze.getContentCards({ timeout: 5000 }); // Option 3: Separate method const cards = await Braze.getContentCardsWithTimeout(5000); ``` Add native timeout support with: - Configurable duration - Proper error handling - Fallback to cache on timeout - Clear timeout vs network error distinction## Additional Context ### Other Information Many other SDKs provide timeout mechanisms: - Firebase: Configurable timeouts - Segment: 30s default timeout - Amplitude: Built-in retry with backoff This feature would greatly improve developer experience and app reliability. 1. Using only `getCachedContentCards()` - But we need fresh data 2. Event-based approach - Still no guarantee of response 3. Manual Promise.race() - Works but feels like a hack Would the team consider adding this feature? Happy to contribute a PR if you provide guidance on the preferred approach.

Benefits for All SDK Users - Promotes cleaner kill switch integration in regulated environments. - Prevents misuse of internal APIs. - Reduces maintenance for integrators. - Provides consistency with existing SDK patterns (handleBrazeRemoteMessage). ### Other Information _No response_

braze-web-sdk #160 [open] [Feature]: zero storage version
### What problem are you facing? The SDK requires either cookies or local storage to function: When using it for analytics, analytics cookie/storage consent must be obtained from the user when GDPR compliance is required. This means that event data will not have full user coverage when using for logged in users where we can obtain consent for analytics via T&Cs. (cookie/localStorage cannot be via T&Cs). ### Workarounds None available for the SDK, have to fallback to implementing something using the braze rest api and a secured proxy to keep api key private. ### Ideal Solution Instead of `noCookie: boolean` option, have a `storage` option e.g. `storage: 'cookie' | 'localStorage' | 'none'`. Requests could be stored in memory and sent in batches until navigation away from page (especially in SPAs) - at which point they would be sent utilising [`visibilitychange` window event ](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Document/visibilitychange_event) and [Beacon API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Beacon_API) . ### Other Information _No response_

braze-swift-sdk #140 [closed] [Feature]: Allow for configuration of line height in InAppMessageView
### What problem are you facing? We have in app messages in our app that use a custom font for the title section. Despite most styling options being available to us when configuring IAPs, we are unable to customize the line height of the title. This line spacing ends up being too large and doesn't match our designs. | Actual | Design | |--------|--------| | <img width="259" alt="image" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e918cea5-c1e2-4648-ad64-a2c1ee5b9ae8"> | <img width="300" alt="image" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8a1b71c4-c2e5-4086-8491-8b896f332589"> | ### Workarounds No workarounds available when using `InAppMessageView`. Because `ModalTextView.Layout` and `ModalTextView.textView` are private, the only workarounds would involve re-creating these UI elements, which seems like overkill for the issue at hand ### Ideal Solution The `ModalTextView` used by `InAppMessageView` has an enum `Layout` containing line spacing configurations: ``` /// Manually-tuned values to get us closer to our visual spec. private enum Layout { static let headerLineSpacingScaleFactor = 0.78 static let messageLineSpacingScaleFactor = 0.47 static let headerMessageSpacingOffset = 1.0 } ``` I believe it would be fairly simple to change this `Layout` private enum to a public struct with the same default values. This way we would be able to inject this `Layout` object and configure our own line spacing throughout the app. However, `lineSpacing` isn't enough in our case, so we'd also appreciate exposing a `lineHeightMultiplier`. This is because lineSpacing only supports positive values, while our design requests a negative line spacing, which is a common design requirement. ### Other Information _No response_

braze-swift-sdk #132 [closed] [Bug]: Adopt Swift Concurrency annotations in public APIs
### Platform iOS ### Platform Version – ### Braze SDK Version 9.3.0 ### Xcode Version Xcode 16 beta (or earlier with Swift feature flags) ### Computer Processor Apple (M1) ### Repro Rate 100% (compile-time) ### Steps To Reproduce The Braze SDK is lacking Swift Concurrency annotations, especially in its delegates. We e.g. _assume_ that `func braze(:shouldOpenURL:) -> Bool` runs on main, given its apparent relation to the respective `UIApplication` and `UISceneDelegate` functions, which are all annotated as `@MainActor`. Similarly, `func braze(:willPresentModalWithContext:)` and many more are obviously UI-related and therefore main-bound in all likelihood, but especially with Xcode 16 and/or Concurrency-related Swift feature flags enabled, the lack of annotations is starting to become a problem. Implementing e.g. `BrazeDelegate` in our app within an instance that itself is annotated as `@MainActor` raises the following warning in Xcode 16: > Main actor-isolated instance method 'braze(_:shouldOpenURL:)' cannot be used to satisfy nonisolated protocol requirement; this is an error in the Swift 6 language mode FixIt suggests 2 options: <img width="536" alt="image" src="https://github.com/braze-inc/braze-swift-sdk/assets/462183/ab04a008-af87-4764-bad7-4c7ff193fd35"> Option 1 isn't feasible because we have code paths in there that do expect to run on main, and to satisfy the compiler, we'd have to introduce asynchronous calls, which doesn't really work given the delegate method expects a synchronous return value. Option 2 is an ok intermediate solution and we'll do that for now, but Swift now has (and has had for a while) tools to turn runtime assumptions into compile-time-checked guarantees, and I believe these should be used – especially since callsites now have to take action (adding `@preconcurrency`) to avoid warnings. ### Expected Behavior We believe that the mentioned APIs (and probably many more) should be annotated as `@MainActor`, and generally, the entire public

braze-swift-sdk #129 [closed] [Feature]: Callback for addAlias Function in Swift SDK for Enhanced Error Handling
### What problem are you facing? we are currently using the Braze Swift SDK in our application and have encountered issues with the addAlias function. Specifically, we have observed instances where the alias is not being registered, but there is no callback or error handling mechanism to inform me of this failure. This lack of feedback makes it challenging to diagnose and address the issue effectively. While using the addAlias function, there are occasions where the alias addition fails silently. Without a callback or error reporting mechanism, it's difficult to determine whether the alias was successfully added or why it failed. This hinders our ability to ensure reliable user identity management within our application. ### Workarounds no clean solution at the moment ### Ideal Solution The `addAlias` function in the Braze Swift SDK be updated to include a callback that provides feedback on the status of the alias addition. This callback should offer: - A success indicator (e.g., a Boolean value). - In case of failure, a reason for the error (e.g., network issues, invalid alias, etc.). Use Case: This feature is essential for scenarios where it is crucial to know if an alias has been successfully added. For example, in applications where user identity management is critical, knowing the outcome of the alias addition allows developers to take appropriate actions based on the result. Folks at Meta would really appreciate it if you could test your libraries against the latest release and report any issues that you find. **This new version enables an interop layer by default**, so hopefully many things will just work, but the more off of the beaten path of a simple module / view that a library goes the more likely it is to encounter possible issues ;) The following gist includes a step by step process for how to test your library and report issues: https://gist.github.com/cipolleschi/82b7a9561b8861330efabbd3eb08c6f5. ### Workarounds None ### Ideal Solution The library supports new architecture and bridgeless in React Native 0.74 ### Other Information _No response_

braze-flutter-sdk #58 [closed] Missing Error Data for Content Card Streams
Presently, when we send a request to `refreshContentCards`, the stream does not return any errors in case the request encounters a failure. In contrast, on iOS, the `refreshContentCards` method does provide the capability to capture failures when refreshing content card data from the stream. Unfortunately, in the Braze Flutter SDK, there is currently no built-in mechanism for handling these errors. The only available option is to delve into platform-specific code and modify the existing Method Channel. Implementing this change would be valuable as it would enable users to observe an error state in the event of a failure in the Braze call, enhancing the overall user experience.

braze-react-native-sdk #226 [closed] [Bug]: Braze.getInitialUrl() doesn't use the callback on Android
### Which Platforms? Android ### Which React Native Version? 0.71.7 ### Which @braze/react-native-sdk SDK version? 6.0.1 ### Repro Rate 100% ### Steps To Reproduce 1. Upgrade `@braze/react-native-sdk` to 6.0.1 2. Use Braze.getInitialUrl() 3. Run Android App ### Expected Behavior Expected `Braze.getInitialUrl()` callback return null value on Android ### Actual Incorrect Behavior `Braze.getInitialUrl()` callback does not return a anything on Android ### Verbose Logs _No response_ ### Additional Information I was using Braze.getInitialURL() for both iOS & Android platforms. We use it with promises: `new Promise(resolve => Braze.getInitialURL(resolve))`. That works well in v5.x.x but when upgrading to `6.0.1` when running on Android it got stuck on the first screen of the app. On iOS worked well. Digging deeper into the code I found that the Android bridge for `6.0.0` has an empty implementation for `getInitialUrl`. (never use the callback) https://github.com/braze-inc/braze-react-native-sdk/blob/21aa2517539eaab86ddae1522377fa32118e748a/android/src/oldarch/com/braze/reactbridge/BrazeReactBridge.kt#L12-L14 And in the JS side, it checks for `this.bridge.getInitialUrl` to be defined, otherwise it call the `callback` function with `null`. Since starting 6.0.0 `getInitialUrl` is defined but does not have any implementation, it seems the callback argument is never called. https://github.com/braze-inc/braze-react-native-sdk/blob/21aa2517539eaab86ddae1522377fa32118e748a/src/braze.js#L48-L62 In the React Native layer I was waiting to that callback but the promise never resolves a value. I think it is due the callback on Android bridge is defined but never uses the callback. Fixed the issue checking if Android or iOS in order to call `Braze.getInitialUrl()`, but it took me a bit to understand the root problem 😅 .

braze-web-sdk #144 [closed] [Feature]: Show a triggered in app message at a later time on a different page
### What problem are you facing? I am unable to delay triggering an in-app message when it would be distracting to the user’s experience. Nor callback passed to `subscribeToInAppMessage`, nor any other Braze SDK function allows us to choose to display the in-app message later. ### Workarounds The workaround is as follows: Store the in-app message, triggered by callback passed to`subscribeToInAppMessage()`, internally. To persist it through page reloads, use either `sessionStorage` or `localStorage`. When it is ready to be shown (as determined by our code), flush it from the storage. It is complicated because: - By delaying the in-app message, we may display it later when we should not, e. g. it becomes outdated or the user is no longer is eligible to receive it. - Braze SDK gives us no information or tools which we could use to determine eligibility. - The code should simulate the behaviour of `beforeInAppMessageDisplayed` and `requestDisplayInAppMessage` methods in iOS and Android SDKs. It is harder for us to implement and maintain this code, since we have less knowledge, unlike Braze SDK team. - The in-app message object needs to be stringified before saving it in storage. That means its constructor prototype is lost. To recover it, we also need to save the prototype information. This adds complexity to our Braze integration code. ### Ideal Solution `beforeInAppMessageDisplayed` and `requestDisplayInAppMessage` functions, that exist in [Android](https://www.braze.com/docs/developer_guide/platform_integration_guides/android/in-app_messaging/customization/custom_listeners/?tab=kotlin#altering-in-app-messages-before-display) and [iOS](https://www.braze.com/docs/developer_guide/platform_integration_guides/ios/in-app_messaging/customization/handing_in_app_display/#overriding-in-app-messages-before-display) SDKs. By utilising them, we could easily tell Braze SDK to delay the in-app messages until we are ready to show them. ### Other Information _No response_

Please provide a function that will work in a similar to [registerAndroidPushToken](https://github.com/braze-inc/braze-react-native-sdk/blob/master/src/braze.js#L154) way, accept an APNs string and call Braze.Notifications.register with token transformed to `Data`. ### Workarounds Since the only way to use `Braze.Notifications.register` is binding to native [didRegisterForRemoteNotificationsWithDeviceToken](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/uikit/uiapplicationdelegate/1622958-application), we can trigger this function by requesting notification permission (even if already granted) with any of requestPermission functions of any permission/notification packages. That's not complicated to implement, but adds a layer of implicity to the codebase. ### Ideal Solution It would be very helpful to have `registerIOSPushToken` on JS side. ### Other Information The source of the problem for us was "Uninstall mea

braze-flutter-sdk #52 [closed] [Bug]: Content card image aspect ratio decode bug
Hey there, just mentioning that there is a bug in the deserialisation logic for the BrazeContentCard.imageAspectRatio property: https://github.com/braze-inc/braze-flutter-sdk/blob/master/lib/braze_plugin.dart#L680 When ratio is an integer, it doesn't meet that condition logic and keeps its default value of 1. Pretty easy to confirm with the following test: ``` // bug not parsing aspect ratio if it is an int final card = BrazeContentCard('{"ar":2}'); expect(card.imageAspectRatio, isNot(2)); // but it parses if it's a double final card2 = BrazeContentCard('{"ar":2.0}'); expect(card2.imageAspectRatio, 2); ``` Quick and simple fix would be to replace that condition logic by: `imageAspectRatioJson is num` Implicit cast will take care of integers upon assignment. I can work around it no problem, but I'd love not having to :) Thanks!

braze-swift-sdk #52 [closed] [Important] Xcode 14.3 RC support
Hi everyone, There is currently a Swift compiler issue preventing us from providing support for Xcode 14.3 RC released today. The Swift team at Apple is aware of this issue, and it's being actively worked on [here](https://github.com/apple/swift/pull/64412). We will be monitoring any new Xcode versions to provide support as soon as possible. We understand that this is inconvenient for many developers who are eager to start using the latest features and improvements in Xcode 14.3 RC. We apologize for any disruption this may cause to your workflow and appreciate your patience as we work to resolve this issue. #### Update 03/24/2023 We have released Xcode 14.3 RC compatible versions of our SDKs in the [braze-inc/braze-swift-sdk-xcode-14-3-preview](https://github.com/braze-inc/braze-swift-sdk-xcode-14-3-preview) repository. You can use this preview repository to release your applications to the App Store using Xcode 14.3 RC. While we wait for the final version of Xcode 14.3 which should resolve the issue, the minimum iOS version supported by the SDKs from the preview repository has been increased to iOS 13. If you need pre-iOS 13 support, please use the main repository with Xcode 14.2.

braze-react-native-sdk #196 [closed] [Bug]: new v2+ iOS installation raises concerns
### Which Platforms? iOS ### Which React Native Version? 0.70 ### Which @braze/react-native-sdk SDK version? 2.0.0 - 3.0.0 ### Description Hello, This is more a regression from v1 rather than a bug. The user here is not the end user but the developer. Currently, the recommended way of installing Braze in v2+ suggests assigning Braze as delegate of the React Bridge. braze-react-native-sdk #193 [closed] [Bug]: v2 doesn't support RN <0.68 on iOS
### Which Platforms? iOS ### Which React Native Version? 0.67.5 ### Which @braze/react-native-sdk SDK version? 2.0.2 ### Repro Rate 100% of the time ### Steps To Reproduce Example: 1. `yarn add @braze/react-native-sdk` 2. Build the app on iOS. ### Expected Behavior the app builds ### Actual Incorrect Behavior the app doesn't build ### Verbose Logs _No response_ ### Additional Information Hi there 👋🏻, v2 is using the version of `RCTBundleURLProvider.jsBundleURLForBundleRoot` that doesn't take a `fallbackResource` as parameter, because the version that does take it has been deprecated. However, that version [is only available from RN 0.68 onwards](https://github.com/facebook/react-native/commit/0912ee179c210fb6b2ed9afbb3f2fbc5fb8a2bb3#), making v2 not compatible with older versions of React Native. I also had to explicitly import `<React/RCTBridgeDelegate.h>` from `BrazeReactBridge/BrazeReactBridge/BrazeReactBridge.h` on [our fork of the library](https://github.com/braze-inc/braze-react-native-sdk/compare/master...justwatch:braze-react-native-sdk:master) to make it work (maybe because our `AppDelegate` doesn't extend the new `RCTAppDelegate`? Not sure, we also had to extend `UIResponder` directly, so it might be specific to us). With those 2 changes in place, our RN 0.67.5-based app builds fine. Thanks!

braze-flutter-sdk #28 [closed] [bug][regression] the new streaming api's broke an existing fix
Some time ago, the "queued messages" was introduced: ```dart /// Sets a callback to receive in-app message data from Braze. @Deprecated( 'Use subscribeToInAppMessages(void onEvent(List<BrazeContentCard> contentCard)) instead.') void setBrazeInAppMessageCallback(Function(BrazeInAppMessage) callback) { _brazeInAppMessageHandler = callback; if (_replayCallbacksConfigEnabled() && _queuedInAppMessages.isNotEmpty) { print("Replaying callback on previously queued Braze in-app messages."); _queuedInAppMessages.forEach((message) => callback(message)); _queuedInAppMessages.clear(); } } ``` Where queued messages got replayed. Now you've introduced the Stream api, which looks like this: ```dart /// Subscribes to the stream of in-app messages and calls [onEvent] when it /// receives an in-app message. StreamSubscription subscribeToInAppMessages( void onEvent(BrazeInAppMessage inAppMessage)) { StreamSubscription subscription = inAppMessageStreamController.stream.listen((inAppMessage) { onEvent(inAppMessage); }); return subscription; } ``` To prove my point, the following: ``` final controller = StreamController<int>.broadcast(); controller.add(1); controller.stream.listen(print); controller.add(2); controller.close(); ``` prints `2`; Thus, queued messages are not replayed.

braze-react-native-sdk #160 [closed] getContentCards returns stale data after calling requestContentCardsRefresh
We are currently using our own implementation for content cards UI, because of this we need to manually refresh the cards. However the `requestContentCardsRefresh` method does not return the value of the api call, so we're required to use the `getContentCards` method to receive the cards. The issue is, because the `requestContentCardsRefresh` method is not await-able, we are receiving the previously cached set of cards. This leaves us with stale data, despite having pulled the most recent set of cards. This can be reproduced by ``` braze.requestContentCardsRefresh(); // this call is not await-able, but performs the asynchronous api call const cards = await braze.getContentCards(); // this call receives the stale data ```

braze-web-sdk #114 [closed] [Feature]: unuglified version
### What problem are you facing? There is no way to know what this is doing. It is bad practice to just include code in your codebase without vetting it, and it is truly impossible to vet in this minified form. I understand that it might lead to people including the non-minified format, and this might be the only acceptable rationale for not publishing it. If Braze is scared for reverse engineering, that is just security through obscurity. By doing it for this reason you're basically saying you need to trust us, but we do not trust you, and we do not have reasonable defenses against people spamming the (undocumented) SDK endpoints. ### Workarounds Tried to http://www.jsnice.org/ but it won't get much better. ### Ideal Solution Open source SDK ### Other Information Please do not be evil.

braze-react-native-sdk #139 [closed] Weird `changeUser()` behavior

I think you need to update react-native SDK as well. https://github.com/Appboy/appboy-android-sdk/blob/64774c3c64b5481e758de8f518ef56bdbdf4432d/CHANGELOG.md#added ``` Added Added the ability to change SDK authentication signature with Braze.changeUser() when the current user id and a new signature is passed in. Previously, Braze.changeUser() would not change the SDK authentication signature if the current user id was used. ```

braze-flutter-sdk #4 [closed] InAppMessages are "swallowed" given the suggested setup

The README suggests the following: > Your beforeInAppMessageDisplayed method implementation should return InAppMessageOperation.DISCARD. For an example, see MainActivity.kt in our example app. So you get something like this: ```kotlin override fun beforeInAppMessageDisplayed(inAppMessage: IInAppMessage): InAppMessageOperation { Handler(Looper.getMainLooper()).post { BrazePlugin.processInAppMessage(inAppMessage) } return InAppMessageOperation.DISCARD } ``` I'm wondering if a setup like the following would be better: ```kotlin override fun beforeInAppMessageDisplayed(inAppMessage: IInAppMessage): InAppMessageOperation { if (!BrazePlugin.canProcessInAppMessages()) { return InAppMessageOperation.DISPLAY_LATER } Handler(Looper.getMainLooper()).post { BrazePlugin.processInAppMessage(inAppMessage) } return InAppMessageOperation.DISCARD } ``` This would mean that the braze plugin can provide this `canProcessInAppMessages` method. Is this a solution that would work for the issue I described?

braze-web-sdk #96 [closed] Massive Package Size
The package is massive by modern standards (50kB gzipped) - larger than `react` and `react-dom` combined - and if you import any part of it you get the entire thing into your application. - It should support ES modules, either via dual exports or just using them exclusively. - It should set the `"sideEffects": false` field in `package.json` so bundlers can know it is side effect free (as long as it actually is?) These things _might_ reduce the size when using bundlers but depending on how the project is set up it might not help. Further reading: https://blog.sindresorhus.com/get-ready-for-esm-aa53530b3f77 https://bundlephobia.com/result?p=@braze/web-sdk@3.2.0

braze-web-sdk #63 [closed] Race condition causes queued events to error out
Based on some research it looks like the `appboyQueue` gets traversed and events executed when the script has been loaded on the browser. Due to this, if something adds a custom event to this queue before the initialize code is called the sdk will throw the error `Appboy must be initialized before calling methods.` See an example [here](https://gist.github.com/gabceb/d499e6cfe5aae53c7f6765bdf9636bf1) As a possible solution to the issue above we could queue up the `initialize` call thus guaranteeing it will be picked up before any other event. The problem with this approach is that the boolean that is returned on the `initialize` event cannot be used because it is picked up from the queue instead of runtime code. As a possible solution, it would be nice to have a global `appboy` property where we could set to defer the execution of the functions on the queue instead of them being picked up when the script is loaded. By doing this we could `initialize` appboy and then on successful initialization we traverse the queue and execute the functions.

braze-web-sdk #59 [closed] Question: Future of `messageReadyCallback`
I see in [this change log](https://github.com/Appboy/appboy-web-sdk/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md#231) that `messageReadyCallback` is being deprecated. However, we've relied on this to ensure the proper timing of events in scenario's where the user is being redirected, and we want to wait for all analytics calls to finish (specifically in our sign up flows). Our order of events is: 1. User submits form 2. User is created (via async API request) 3. Data is received from user creation, which we use to send to braze via `appboy.changeUser` 4. Redirect. If we don't have a way to wait for the async`changeUser` call to finish, then we risk missing some of those calls, since a redirect will force ongoing requests to be canceled. So will there be another way to wait for that call to finish? Or can you reconsider the fate of the `messageReadyCallback`?

braze-web-sdk #56 [closed] Issue with CSP rule "style-src 'self'"
We use a Content Security Policy with "[style-src](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Content-Security-Policy/style-src) 'self';" that causes violations when the braze sdk attempts to load the font awesome style sheets. We are working around the issue by using the `doNotLoadFontAwesome` configuration option but it would be great if the sdk were updated to be compatibility with this rule. While the current means of loading the styles is not supported, styles can still be added programmatically with our policy using alternative methods, though the easiest solution might be to give us the ability to specify a NONCE when we initialize the sdk.

braze-web-sdk #39 [closed] appboy.openSession throws an exception when in an Iframe on safari
I'm seeing the error described in this stackoverflow question when calling appboy.openSession: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/39712455/indexdb-dom-exception-18-security-ios-10-iframe As part of Safari's "Intelligent Tracking Prevention" they basically disable third party cookies in an Iframe when the user has not visited the page outside of an Iframe previously. Appears that this is also the case for access for IndexedDB. The MDN article does note: > Third party window content (e.g. <iframe> content) can access the IndexedDB store for the origin it is embedded into, unless the browser is set to never accept third party cookies (see bug 1147821.) https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/IndexedDB_API/Using_IndexedDB#Security Looks like you need a check to see if you can set third party cookies, and if not fall back to another storage medium.

braze-web-sdk #12 [closed] Callback Method Signature Inconsistency
There's a bit of inconsistency in the current API with respect to where you pass callbacks: - [isPushGranted(yesCallback, noCallback, safariWebsitePushId)](https://js.appboycdn.com/web-sdk/1.6/doc/module-appboy.html#.isPushGranted) - [registerAppboyPushMessages(successCallback, deniedCallback, safariWebsitePushId)](https://js.appboycdn.com/web-sdk/1.6/doc/module-appboy.html#.registerAppboyPushMessages) - [submitFeedback(replyToEmail, message, isReportingABug, successCallback, errorCallback)](https://js.appboycdn.com/web-sdk/1.6/doc/module-appboy.html#.submitFeedback) It seems like callback params should be passed at the beginning or end of the function in a consistent way. #11 could definitely help here because passing `safariWebsitePushId` to `isPushGranted` and `registerAppboyPushMessages` as a param could be deprecated and, moving forward, the pattern is that sucess and fail params are always the last two params in the method signature. Originally discussed here: https://github.com/blimmer/ember-appboy/issues/27#issuecomment-251697548

braze-web-sdk #9 [closed] Expose way to stub internal redirect method

If it's an external link, I don't wire this up and let the SDK handle it. I'm running into some problems writing a test for this behavior because `window.location =` is not stub-able. It looks like there's a method used internally to do the redirect: ``` javascript c.ga.xd (a, c, d) { d || null != c && c.metaKey ? window.open(a) : window.location = a } ``` I can simulate a meta keypress but, ideally, I'd stub out this whole method and confirm that it was called. braze-web-sdk #7 [closed] Feature Request: Automated Testing Mode

Additionally, this could cause initialization with fake API keys that cause noise to the Appboy servers. For example, I have lots of tests in [ember-appboy](https://github.com/blimmer/ember-appboy/blob/master/tests/unit/instance-initializers/appboy-test.js#L30-L34) that require a significant amount of stubbing. What about something like: ``` javascript appboy.initialize('API-KEY', { automatedTesting: true }); ``` Then, I could check the app environment and merge the `automatedTesting` key into the options object at initialization time.
